confirmed_defect.description: The optional AVG update builder passes a named intrusive pointer to a NewLambda overload that requires an rvalue body pointer.
confirmed_defect.minimal_repair: Move the update body pointer into NewLambda at its sole consuming call.

repair_contracts: TExprContext::NewLambda(TPositionHandle, TExprNode::TPtr&&, TExprNode::TPtr&&) forwards ownership of both pointers into the expression node.
The local update body pointer has no read or write after the call; moving it cannot invalidate a later local use.

The lambda body retains references to stateArg and the nested input lambda; NewArguments retains the matching argument nodes. Moving the outer body pointer does not change argument identity or lexical binding.
The prospective repair changes exactly one production line and needs no yql/essentials edits.
surrounding_contracts_reviewed: IntervalType removes optionality before testing the data slot. Interval and Interval64 widen through Int64 into Decimal(35,0); numeric and Decimal AVG retain their existing conversion path.

Optional initialization produces either an optional sum/count tuple or Nothing of the same tuple type. Optional updates ignore null input, preserve a present state on null input, and initialize from the input when the state is absent.
Final-phase updates merge existing sum/count states rather than converting the whole input tuple as a scalar interval.

Intermediate finish returns the state unchanged. Final interval finish divides the widened sum by Uint64 count and converts through Int64 back to the original interval family, matching established aggregate traits.
Optional interval finish wraps only the present result and produces Nothing of Optional<original interval family> for absent state.

Decimal-backed tuple recovery is restricted to final AVG traits. The existing union/partial binding map recovers original interval versus Decimal input type, while input optionality is retained separately for the finish wrapper.
Ordinary propagated final aggregates retain original logical input types; union-based DISTINCT states use tuple recovery. DISTINCT padding removes optionality before accessing the interval data slot.
No additional production defect was established by this source review.
coverage_limits: No compilation or native execution was performed by this reviewer. The amended commit must pass the guarded build and runtime checks before acceptance.
Existing row-oriented small single-node profiles do not by themselves establish distributed merge or block-path coverage.
Optional/all-null/empty inputs, multiple DISTINCT interval states, whole-partition window expansion and numeric/Decimal controls remain required runtime checks.
C34 separately owns general tuple-valued empty-state handling. C24/C26 touch DISTINCT padding and F02 owns interval SUM; independent source review does not prove combined-branch behavior.
The inherited Decimal(35,0) accumulation precision and Uint64 count limits remain unchanged.
